strongest_frame: 12.8 s (frame 384): a close shot of the authored station housing and solar panel beside the creek. A diagonal sunbeam has just struck the panel, the 'Charges from light' callout is pinned and the battery meter has gone from one orange bar (12.0 s) to four green bars. The creek water carries mirrored tree reflections. One finished hero object performs a readable cause and result above the caption band.
weakest_frame: 18.0 s (frame 540), in the declared signature shot s3-event-2. An opaque flat brown rectangle fills about 60 percent of the frame and has swallowed the lower sensor pods; only two dark pods remain visible and no lens lights. A sliver of grass and creek shows at the lower right corner, revealing the slab as a hard-edged overlay rather than water. The caption 'Four optical sensors at different heights watch the water.' sits over it while the picture never shows four sensors or any watching.
notes: One-viewing reconstruction before the rationale: an illustrated San Antonio backyard is followed by a phone that gets a flash flood warning, then a solar station on a post. Its panel charges, a cell tower is labelled not needed, sensor pods sit on the pole, an opened box shows a TinyML chip lighting up, radio rings leave the antenna, an arc reaches a hub mast, a desk monitor shows a chart with orange blobs, text cards report 98.82% validation accuracy and no field result, a blank map gets a no-installation tag, and a dashed outline of an uninstalled station closes the film. Input, action and result in plain words: sensor readings go into a chip on the station, the chip lights a risk lamp, and a radio signal reaches a hub. The solar charge (12.0 to 12.8 s), the chip glow (21.8 to 24.8 s), the mast landing (33.0 to 33.4 s) and the dashed closing outline (56.6 to 57.4 s) are genuinely pictured. The opening stakes (water before warning), the four-sensor water crossing, the street-range travel, the flood-path map and the hub responder are absent, contradicted or carried by labels. Region is correct (Bexar, San Antonio skyline, live oaks). On-screen figures 98.82%, half-mile and five miles match verified quotes c4 and c6. Disclosures are visible on every scene; one disclosure mismatch at 8.2 to 8.8 s. All blocking defects are consolidated into one correction below, preserving the story order, narration and measured timing.

consolidated_correction: One correction that keeps the story order, narration, measured timing and source limits. (1) s1: perform real floodwater with the creek's finished reflective treatment, visibly rising over the curb and up the post to the orange ankle mark by 1.0 s. Stage the boots and the waterline on them above the caption band. (2) s3, the hero: show four lenses at four heights, with a water surface and waterline (not a slab) rising past them, each lens lighting as it is crossed, and remove the seam. (3) s4: make the local judgment a large readable state change on the station, and stage the dark server contrast at readable size in the same frame as the station. (4) s5: send the rings down the street to a visible receiving point at a believable scale, or use a map inset with a scale bar. Keep the station as the source in the hub shot, and use a region-correct open view without the downtown skyline for 'open country'. (5) s6: draw an actual street and creek flood map (it can share the s8 map's streets) with paths spreading along the creek and low streets. Replace the rigid disembodied arm with a complete, coherently performing figure or remove it, and fill the blank lower frame. (6) s7 and s8: compress the card time and keep the place visible. One option is to put the validation figure and blank field card in the same hub or curb world. (7) s8 and s9: hold the search sweep long enough to read, keep the no-installation tag pinned to the map, and either draw the promised goal pin or drop it from the board. Previously correct actions to keep: the panel charge, the phone banner, the chip pulse, the mast landing and the dashed closing outline.

blocking_defects: Opening stakes absent in picture (0.0 to 3.8 s): no recognizable yard water, so the 'warning arrives after the water' question is caption-only.
Central mechanism not performed (15.8 to 18.4 s): three pods, not four, a flat brown slab with no lens lighting, and a seam.
Turn too small to read (19.8 to 26.8 s): the risk lamp is a tiny dot and the server contrast is nearly invisible.
Range scale and setting contradict the words (27.2 to 35.0 s): rings in the sky, a short street tagged half-mile, a skyline behind 'open country'.

Text-panel stall (41.0 to 52.0 s) in the limit section.
story_review.one_viewing_summary: UT San Antonio's illustrated solar flood station charges itself from sunlight, a chip inside lights up when readings arrive, and its radio signal reaches a hub mast. Cards then say the only proof is 98.82% validation accuracy, with no field result and no installed town, and the film ends on a dashed outline of a station nobody has installed yet. After one viewing it is not clear that the opening yard is flooding, or what the hub chart shows.
story_review.opening_to_ending: The film opens on a dry-looking yard and a phone that gets a late flood warning, and closes on the same kind of San Antonio curb with a dashed uninstalled station and a 'Deployment goal' tag. The ending honestly answers the limit (design yes, installation none). The opening question about street water is only weakly pictured, because the flooding it depends on never reads as water.
story_review.weakest_transition: s6 to s7 at 40.8 to 41.0 s. The cut goes from the abstract beige-room monitor chart to a flat olive validation card with an empty bar. No subject, place or object carries across; the board's carried amber accent is not a visible bridge. The film switches from mechanism picture to text slideshow here and stays there until 52.0 s.
